title: Coefficient comparison of the etale stratum internal-adjunction pairing
statement:
Fix $k=\overline{\mathbf F}_q$ of characteristic $p$, $\ell\ne p$, a finite extension $E/\mathbf Q_\ell$, a uniformizer $\varpi_E$, and $n\ge m\ge1$. Set $A=\mathcal O_E/(\varpi_E^n)$ and $B=\mathcal O_E/(\varpi_E^m)$. Let $X$ be separated of finite type over $k$ and let $s=gj:S\hookrightarrow X$ factor as an open immersion $j:S\hookrightarrow Z$ followed by a closed immersion $g:Z\hookrightarrow X$. Work on small etale sites with ordinary uncompleted derived module categories. Write $F_T=-\otimes_A^LB$, $H_A=R\mathcal Hom_A$, and $s_A^!=j^*Rg_A^!$, $s_{!,A}=g_{*,A}j_!$, and similarly over $B$. Let $M\in D^b_{ctf}(X_{\mathrm{et}},A)$, $L\in D^b_{ctf}(S_{\mathrm{et}},A)$, $N=s_A^!M$, and $Q=H_A(L,N)$. Assume $N,Q$ are finite-Tor bounded constructible. Let $I_A:Rs_{*,A}Q\xrightarrow{\sim}H_A(s_{!,A}L,M)$ be canonical internal adjunction: its transpose is the pairing
$$Rs_{*,A}Q\otimes_A^Ls_{!,A}L\longrightarrow s_{!,A}(s^*Rs_{*,A}Q\otimes_A^LL)\xrightarrow{s_!(\alpha_A\otimes1)}s_{!,A}(Q\otimes_A^LL)\xrightarrow{s_!\mathrm{ev}_A}s_{!,A}N\xrightarrow{\epsilon_{s,A}}M,$$
where the first arrow is the inverse compact-support projection isomorphism formed from the open tensor and closed proper projection maps, and $\alpha_A:s^*Rs_{*,A}Q\to Q$ is the ordinary counit. Define $I_B$ by the same pairing over $B$.

Let $c_{s,Q}$ be the ordinary counit-defined coefficient comparison. Let $q_s$ be the compact-support comparison obtained by composing the canonical open comparison with the closed direct-image comparison, and let $b_{s,M}:F_SN\xrightarrow{\sim}s_B^!F_XM$ satisfy
$$\epsilon_{s,B}\circ s_{!,B}(b_{s,M})\circ q_{s,N}=F_X\epsilon_{s,A}.$$
Let $u:F_SQ\to H_B(F_SL,F_SN)$ be the transpose of coefficient change of evaluation. Then the following equality of maps from $F_XRs_{*,A}Q$ to $H_B(F_Xs_{!,A}L,F_XM)$ holds:
$$H_B(q_{s,L},1)\circ I_B\circ Rs_{*,B}(H_B(1,b_{s,M})\circ u)\circ c_{s,Q}=v_{s_{!,A}L,M}\circ F_XI_A,$$
where $v$ is the evaluation-defined coefficient comparison (with no invertibility assumed). In particular this equality identifies the composite internal-adjunction comparison with the specified evaluation transpose, rather than merely identifying its endpoints.

Notation and categorical conventions are those of [def-weil-finite-field-fiber], [def-weil-l-adic-coefficient-extension], [def-weil-scheme-morphism-properties], [def-weil-pbc-derived-categories], [def-weil-pbc-constructible-complexes], [def-kun-tor-amplitude], [def-pur-derived-internal-hom], [lem-pur-derived-change-of-rings], [def-amb-etale-compact-support], [lem-exc-closed-ambient], [def-kun-projection-formula-map], [lem-coef-etale-open-tensor].

source.place: Proof paragraph 4, "Every comparison used is defined by the same evaluations and adjunction counits; transposing identifies their composite"; extracted returned step 8

proof.text: Notation: for $T\in D(X_{\mathrm{et}},A)$ and $L$ as in the statement, $\Pi_A(T,L):T\otimes_A^Ls_{!,A}L\xrightarrow{\sim}s_{!,A}(s^*T\otimes_A^LL)$ is the proper projection $T\otimes g_*j_!L\to g_*(g^*T\otimes j_!L)$ followed by $g_*(\gamma^{-1}_{L,g^*T})$, as in the statement; similarly $\Pi_B$. Open square: for $T'\in D(Z_{\mathrm{et}},A)$ the two maps $F_Zj_!(L\otimes j^*T')\to j_!F_SL\otimes_BF_ZT'$ given by $\gamma_B\circ j_!(\text{tensor identification})\circ q_{j,L\otimes j^*T'}$ and $(q_{j,L}\otimes1)\circ F_Z(\gamma_A)$ are equal. Indeed $q_j$ is invertible, so it suffices to compare them after precomposing with $q^{-1}$; both are then maps out of $j_!(\cdot)$, hence determined by their $j_!\dashv j^*$ adjuncts on $S$, and both adjuncts are the canonical restriction/tensor identification, because $\gamma$ is the adjunct of that identification and $q_{j,P}$ restricts to the identity. The associativity identifications are the canonical ones of [lem-coef-etale-open-tensor].

source.place: Proof paragraph 4, Every comparison used is defined by the same evaluations and adjunction counits

proof.text: Proper square for $g$, applied to the pushed object $P=j_!L$ and $T\in D(X_{\mathrm{et}},A)$ (not to $Q$, which lives on $S$). Let $c_{g,P}:F_Xg_{*,A}P\to g_{*,B}F_ZP$ be the closed direct-image comparison that is the first factor of $q_{s,L}=g_{*,B}(q_{j,L})\circ c_{g,j_!L}$ [lem-coef-etale-locally-closed-shriek]; its $g^*\dashv g_{*}$ transpose over $B$ is $F_Z(\epsilon^{g}_{A,P})$ after $g^*F_X\cong F_Zg^*$ (definition in [lem-coef-finite-direct-image] and [lem-coef-etale-locally-closed-shriek]). The proper projection $\mathrm{pr}(T,P):T\otimes g_*P\to g_*(g^*T\otimes P)$ has transpose $1\otimes\epsilon^g_P$. Compare $c_{g,g^*T\otimes P}\circ F_X\mathrm{pr}_A(T,P)$ and $\mathrm{pr}_B(F_XT,F_ZP)\circ(1\otimes c_{g,P})$ through their $B$-transposes $g^*F_X(T\otimes g_*P)\to F_Z(g^*T\otimes P)$: the first is $F_Z(\epsilon^g)\circ g^*F_X\mathrm{pr}_A=F_Z(1\otimes\epsilon^g_P)$ by naturality of the counit transpose; the second is $(1\otimes\epsilon^g_{B})\circ(1\otimes g^*c_{g,P})=1\otimes F_Z(\epsilon^g_P)$. They agree under the monoidal identification $g^*F_X(T\otimes g_*P)\cong g^*F_XT\otimes F_Zg^*g_*P$, so the proper square commutes.

source.place: Proof paragraph 4, Every comparison used is defined by the same evaluations and adjunction counits

proof.text: Paste Step 1 (with $T'=g^*T$), applied under $g_{*,B}$, with Step 2, using naturality of $c_{g,\cdot}$ to move $F_Xg_*(\gamma_A^{-1})$ past it [lem-coef-finite-direct-image]. Since $q_{s,L}=g_{*,B}(q_{j,L})\circ c_{g,j_!L}$ [lem-coef-etale-locally-closed-shriek], this gives, for every $T\in D(X_{\mathrm{et}},A)$, the compact-support projection square $$\Pi_B(F_XT,F_SL)\circ(1\otimes q_{s,L})=s_{!,B}(\iota)\circ q_{s,s^*T\otimes L}\circ F_X\Pi_A(T,L)$$ as maps $F_X(T\otimes s_{!,A}L)\to s_{!,B}(s^*F_XT\otimes F_SL)$, where $\iota:F_S(s^*T\otimes L)\cong s^*F_XT\otimes F_SL$ is the canonical restriction/tensor identification and $F_X(T\otimes s_!L)\cong F_XT\otimes F_Xs_!L$ is used on the source. No counit $\alpha$ and no $c_{s,Q}$ enter this square; they are treated in Step 6.

source.place: Proof paragraph 4, Every comparison used is defined by the same evaluations and adjunction counits

proof.text: The final exceptional-counit square is the displayed hypothesis on b_{s,M}: epsilon_{s,B} composed with s_{!,B}(b_{s,M}) and q_{s,N} equals F_X(epsilon_{s,A}). Therefore, once the preceding projection square has been applied, the last counit in the B pairing is exactly the coefficient change of the last counit in the A pairing. No pro-etale closed-shriek result is needed here, since this identity is part of the ordinary-etale statement being proved.

source.place: Proof paragraph 4, Every comparison used is defined by the same evaluations and adjunction counits

proof.text: Let ev_u:F_SQ tensor_B F_SL to F_SN be the transpose of u. By the defining transpose condition for u, ev_u is the coefficient change of ev_A under the canonical scalar-extension and tensor-associativity maps. Thus the middle evaluation arrow in the B pairing, after the coefficient comparisons, is exactly F_S of the middle evaluation arrow in the A pairing.

source.place: Proof paragraph 4, Every comparison used is defined by the same evaluations and adjunction counits

proof.text: Put $h=Rs_{*,B}(w)\circ c_{s,Q}$ with $w=H_B(1,b_{s,M})\circ u$. Since $I_B$ is the internal adjunction whose transpose is the stated pairing, [lem-asd-internal-adjunction-evaluation] (for $s=gj$, finite ring $B$) gives the transpose of $I_B\circ h$ as $\epsilon_{s,B}\circ s_{!,B}(p)\circ\Pi_B(F_XRs_{*,A}Q,F_SL)$, where $p:s^*F_XRs_{*,A}Q\otimes F_SL\to s_B^!F_XM$ is the transpose of $h$, i.e. $p=\mathrm{ev}_B\circ((w\circ\alpha_B\circ s^*c_{s,Q})\otimes1)$. By the definition of $c_{s,Q}$ [lem-coef-finite-direct-image], $\alpha_B\circ s^*c_{s,Q}=F_S(\alpha_A)$ after $s^*F_X\cong F_Ss^*$. By Step 5 and naturality of evaluation in the target, $\mathrm{ev}_B\circ(w\otimes1)=b_{s,M}\circ\mathrm{ev}_u=b_{s,M}\circ F_S(\mathrm{ev}_A)$. Hence $p=b_{s,M}\circ F_S(e_A)\circ\iota^{-1}$ with $e_A=\mathrm{ev}_A\circ(\alpha_A\otimes1)$. The transpose of the left side is this map precomposed with $1\otimes q_{s,L}$. Step 3 with $T=Rs_{*,A}Q$ rewrites it as $\epsilon_{s,B}\circ s_{!,B}(b_{s,M})\circ s_{!,B}F_S(e_A)\circ q_{s,s^*T\otimes L}\circ F_X\Pi_A$; naturality of $q_s$ [lem-coef-etale-locally-closed-shriek] gives $s_{!,B}F_S(e_A)\circ q=q_{s,N}\circ F_Xs_{!,A}(e_A)$, and Step 4 turns $\epsilon_{s,B}\circ s_{!,B}(b_{s,M})\circ q_{s,N}$ into $F_X\epsilon_{s,A}$. So the transpose is $F_X(\epsilon_{s,A}\circ s_{!,A}(e_A)\circ\Pi_A)$, i.e. $F_X$ of the $A$ pairing defining $I_A$.

source.place: Proof paragraph 4, Every comparison used is defined by the same evaluations and adjunction counits

proof.text: Transpose of the right side: by the evaluation normalization of $v$ (its $B$-transpose is $F_X(\mathrm{ev}_A)$ under $F_X(H\otimes P)\cong F_XH\otimes F_XP$, as in [lem-sfb-dc-hom-scalar-adjunction]) and naturality of the tensor--Hom bijection, the transpose of $v_{s_{!,A}L,M}\circ F_XI_A$ is $F_X(\mathrm{ev}_A\circ(I_A\otimes1))=F_X$ of the transpose of $I_A$, which by the definition of $I_A$ (equivalently [lem-asd-internal-adjunction-evaluation] with $h=1$) is $F_X(\epsilon_{s,A}\circ s_{!,A}(e_A)\circ\Pi_A)$. This is the map obtained in Step 6. No inverse of $v$ is used.

source.place: Proof paragraph 4, Every comparison used is defined by the same evaluations and adjunction counits

proof.text: The representing Hom-bijections for the ordinary tensor–Hom adjunction are bijective, so two maps are equal when their transposes are equal. Applying this to the common transpose computed in Steps 6 and 7 proves the displayed equality. Only canonical associativity, restriction, and scalar-extension identifications were used.

split_report.summary: Proof of the pairing-change equality by transposition. Steps 1-3 prove the compact-support projection square for the actual projection (closed proper projection of g on j_!L, then the inverse open tensor map), with the closed comparison c_{g,j_!L} that is the first factor of q_{s,L}. Step 4 is the assumed exceptional-counit identity, Step 5 the evaluation normalization of u. Step 6 computes the transpose of the left side, handling the c_{s,Q}/counit square and the naturality of q_s. Step 7 computes the transpose of the right side, and Step 8 concludes from the Hom-bijection. No closed-shriek pro-etale theorem is used. Maintainer reader (Q111) corrected steps 2, 3, 6 and 7: step 2 had used c_{g,Q} instead of c_{g,j_!L}, and the counit square for c_{s,Q} and the naturality of q_s were implicit.

lean.note: The canonical open/closed operations are expanded in helpers: ordinary direct image is Rg_* Rj_* through the canonical composition identification. The internal-adjunction arrow is constructed by transposing the specified proper/open projection, ordinary counit, evaluation and pasted exceptional counit. Evaluation comparison uses the published normalized etaleHomTensorComparison; b is an isomorphism subject exactly to the displayed exceptional-counit hypothesis. No invertibility of the Hom comparison is assumed.
